title: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly
description: For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row 's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently. Read more

title: Get 31 Cyberpunk 2077 And The Witcher Comics Or Books At A 95% Discount In This Bundle
description: CD Projekt Red’s Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 are some of the best RPGs ever made thanks to an engrossing pair of worlds filled with lovable (and hateable) characters. I mean, how can you not love Panam, hate Adam Smasher, love Geralt, and hate the Bloody Baron? If you want to expand your love of these two worlds, this comics bundle gives you plenty of material to broaden your Night City or Continent horizons at a huge 95% off, saving you hundreds of bucks. For instance, The World of Cyberpunk 2077—a book I have opened up too many times to count—is a stunning look into the dystopian world, with concept art that sees Night City shine, from afar to the dingy nooks and crannies of this legendary location. On the other hand, the Trauma Team comic brings all four parts together, seeing the city through the eyes of an EMT working for Trauma Team International. Each of the Cyberpunk 2077 comics follows different lives in the City of Dreams, dragging you through the dirt and grime of the game's setting in unique ways that you don't experience as V. As someone who has been getting deeply involved with the Cyberpunk TCG, I've found myself looking beyond the game's narrative and getting to grips with the lore. I've also found myself falling in love with the world even more, especially after reading some of the comics. I truly recommend the Big City Dreams comic; go in blind, and you'll soon fall in love with it, too. While the Cyberpunk books expand your view of Night City in general, The Witcher books follow a variety of adventures with the lovable monster-hunting Geralt. While some of them are based on short stories by Andrzej Sapkowski himself, others take a different approach, like House of Glass, which sees The Witcher entering the titular mansion, with endless rooms and horrors waiting around every corner. Normally, this 31-book collection would set you back $411.61 / £308.20. That's a lot of money, but you're getting hours of reading for that price. However, right…

title: New Ubisoft Boss Wants Studio To Become “A24 Of Video Games”
description: Ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2. In a new interview, Hartmann talked about his hopes for the unit, saying his dream would be for it to become "like the A24 of video games." He told Variety that what he means by this is that Creative House 2 can be like A24 in that it can make games that are both critically and commercially successful. A24's biggest hit ever was this year's Backrooms, which made more than $400 million worldwide against a reported budget of $10 million and was received positively by fans and critics. Some of A24's other recent big critical and commercial hits have included Marty Supreme ($192 million), Everything Everywhere All at Once ($148 million), The Drama ($135 million), and Civil War ($127 million). Jesse Plemons in A24's Civil War. Saying Ubisoft's Creative House 2 could aim for what A24 is doing is certainly an ambitious goal, and it's not the first time that Hartmann has made such a bold claim about what he's working on. When he was at Amazon, Hartmann said his objective was to help Amazon become “the Disney of the future,” with gaming standing alongside TV, film, music, and retail. Creative House 2 covers franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon, Splinter Cell, and March of Giants (which Ubisoft bought from Hartmann's previous company, Amazon). "Hartmann’s role is to oversee strategic direction and development of the studios and brands under Creative House 2," Ubisoft said. Hartmann told Variety that he wants Creative House 2 to "definitely not" be a place that only makes shooter games. "I want us to be a label which really looks after the core gamer. And what I mean by that, it’s almost easier to describe what we’re not going to do. So I’m not going to do a racing game. I’m not going to do sports. I’m not going to do a casual kids title. But could we do an RPG one day? Could we do MMO? Could I maybe do even a strategy game? Sure, it’s all coming down to…

title: Ocarina Of Time Is 2026’s Best-Selling Physical Game In The US, But GTA 6 Is Coming
description: Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 is the best-selling physical game of 2026, according to Circana, but GTA 6 is coming out soon and could topple that record. Circana's Mat Piscatella said the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 was the first game to surpass 1 million physical units sold in the US for its launch week since 2023's The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 released on November 5, and Circana's reporting period ended on November 7, so the achievement was actually accomplished in just two days, not even a full week. Ocarina of Time's physical edition, which includes a cartridge, sells for $70, compared to $60 for its digital counterpart. GTA 6 launches on November 19, and while the game is fully digital, Rockstar is releasing a "physical" version of the game at brick-and-mortar retailers. Buyers don't get a disc--only a code for the game. In any event, for Circana, code-in-a-box games are considered new physical game sales, so GTA 6 is no doubt going to topple Ocarina of Time's record. Ocarina of Time's remake for Switch 2 sold more than 5 million copies over its first four days globally. The latest sales data for GTA 6 pre-purchases show that the game has passed 16 million units sold worldwide.

title: Deadlock Has Convinced Me We Should All Be Role-Playing In Competitive Games
description: Every time I enter the team lobby in Deadlock, I start a match by sending one message: “HI IM REM.” Rem is a rat/crow/cat-looking fantasy critter in Valve's online team-based shooter Deadlock. The game blends genre elements from both team-based hero shooters and multiplayer online battle arena games. The developers still describe it as being in “early development,” but it’s already widely popular. Deadlock had more than 300,000 concurrent players on Steam in October, according to SteamDB, and the game has already inspired a vibrant fandom on social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram. In Deadlock, players fight 6v6 in a fantasy New York setting called the Cursed Apple. The game has a pretty flexible concept thematically, so it allows for all kinds of quirky characters. As of writing, the current selection of playable heroes includes characters like a park pigeon lady, an angsty teen who goes to a fancy private school and wields a lich hand, a literal rat king who wants to take over Long Island, and then of course, there is my boy Rem. His backstory is that he is a childlike creature who is lost and trying to find his way home. Instead of fighting with a gun, he uses a candlestick and pillow to push his opponents. Since it’s an online game where I play with other people, Deadlock uses both voice chat and text team chat. When I start a new match, I introduce myself as Rem. It started as a bit; I saw a video where people joked about how Deadlock players tend to take on the characteristics of their mains. However, it soon stuck, and I would use the team chat to act as Rem as I played with strangers. Whenever I needed to communicate in chat, I would do so in the voice of my character. So instead of saying, “Be right back,” I would mimic his childlike voice and send messages like, “Rem will hurry back,” or if I missed an ability I might say, “REM TRIED TO GET THERE IN TIME.” As I play, it almost feels like the design of the game encourages lighthearted ways of…

title: Sony Is Updating The PS5 Again, And It Might Have GTA 6 Pirates In Mind
description: A new PS5 firmware update has dropped, but even at a chunky 1.2GB download, version 26.07-14.23.00 doesn't include a comprehensive list of notes. "We've made some security fixes to the system software," the very short update notes read. Notably, this is the fourth PS5 firmware update since October 1, and typically there's a buffer period of several months between downloads. While Sony hasn't confirmed it, the current thinking is that the company is shoring up its defenses for the release of GTA 6 to prevent the game from being pirated. The new firmware will be mandatory for new game releases as well, including GTA 6, which means that PS5 hackers and homebrew hobbyists have their work cut out for them. The hacking scene recently made big advances on the console, jailbreaking systems that have update 14 and below installed, and thus allowing more pirated games to be played. Sony is under pressure to prevent GTA 6 from being pirated, and with the PS5 console holding the lion's share of GTA 6 preorders, there's plenty of financial incentive to keep the game secure on that platform. Security researchers and hackers have been leveraging generative AI and automated decompilation analysis to discover lower-level system vulnerabilities and dump game binaries much faster, creating an arms race between Sony and hackers. Every time a potential vulnerability or homebrew exploit surfaces--like the recent vulnerabilities that targeted PS5 consoles running 13.60 and 14.22 firmware--Sony rushes out a mandatory console patch to plug the hole. Beyond security measures, we've also seen base PS5 consoles updated with Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), which is also rolling out to more games. An AI-based upscaling technology derived from the PS5 Pro's PSSR, it initially supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei.

title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI
description: As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike. The manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself. It's a solid entry in the Aliens franchise if you don't mind some base-management chores, as it nails the atmosphere of the classic sequel while giving you plenty of acid-blooded bugs to mow down. title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
description: It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper. The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything. title: How HoYoverse Is Keeping Petit Planet’s AI NPCs From Harassing Players
description: As generative AI enters live-service games, conversational NPCs present exciting creative possibilities for those who choose to use them. However, it also presents a serious moderation challenge. In HoYoverse's upcoming cozy life sim Petit Planet, players can visit a local cafe run by an AI-driven NPC called Nalo. Nalo will remember past conversations and use them to deliver dynamic, personalized responses. However, during closed beta testing, some unsettling interactions involving heavy or self-destructive topics of conversation were noticed. Speaking to GameSpot at HoYoverse's recent media week in Seoul, South Korea, developers Yinli Huang and Murphy addressed safety concerns, outlining how the studio is combining a series of moderation systems to ensure player safety. When asked how the studio plans to prevent self-destructive prompts from slipping through, developer Yinli Huang emphasized that Nalo is not an open-ended chatbot, saying, "There are two sets of systems behind those neighbors. First of all, the NPCs that use the AI system, such as Nalo, will have a preset moral value and personality. As the relationship develops along with the players, it will develop a more customized interaction based on the input of each player." Because Nalo has such a strict moral compass, she will actively shut down toxic or manipulative prompts instead of blindly trying to appease the player. "Once players have said something inappropriate, Nalo will decline to respond to those requests or interact further," Huang explained. The developers recognize that the character's refusal alone may not deter bad actors, nor does it support distressed players who may be using those systems to turn to someone when they need help. To address those problems, HoYoverse built a tiered escalation system into the game. "If that kind of interaction continues, we will put more limits [on] the player, such as a pop-up window notification and human intervention as needed," Murphy explained. These…

title: GTA 6 Has Teamed Up With The Weather Channel To Show How Dynamic Leonida Can Be
description: Rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6' s most impressive features: The Weather Channel. The US broadcaster has shared an exclusive look at Leonida's weather system via six new screenshots and forecasts that make the fictional destination sound like somewhere you'd need to check the weather before visiting. It's an unusual collaboration, but a very fitting one. GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, where sunshine, torrential rain, thunderstorms and tropical storms are all part of the ecosystem. Who better to show off the unpredictable climate than The Weather Channel? The broadcaster posted the collaboration on X, writing "Nobody knows weather like we do. That's why Rockstar gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI." Instead of just posting the six new screenshots, The Weather Channel provided six different weather reports for the various locations across Leonida. Each has its own conditions and some local facts, making the entire post sound like a genuine forecast. The reports include heavy rain reducing visibility across the Keys, a thunderstorm rolling over the swamps of Pelican Valley--and obscuring some feisty "nippers" at the same time--and sea fog threatening to obscure the expensive beachfront views at South Ocean Beach. There's also a tropical storm making the waters around the Rusty Anchor particularly choppy, and Gambit Bay has a low-lying morning mist ahead of hunting season. One forecast warns commuters traveling from Key Lento to expect more rain and wind. It seems like an almost mundane detail for a game about a pair of criminals, but it's this exact impressive world-building that makes Leonida feel real. The six new screenshots are especially impressive, showing off the towering storm clouds and lightning strikes through to dense fog that makes entire stretches of the coastline disappear. Rockstar isn't treating weather as just a visual…

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
description: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. Read more

title: How To Play GTA 6 Early On Xbox Using This Trick
description: Due to GTA 6's non-simultaneous release, people in New Zealand will be the first in the world to play the highly anticipated open-world crime game when it releases at midnight local time there. If you want to become a Kiwi for a day and you plan to play on Xbox, you can trick your console into thinking it's in New Zealand to play early. The following trick has worked before, but there is no guarantee that it will work for you this time with GTA 6, or you might not want to do it at all. After all, Microsoft's own policy says people should only change their region if they have moved to a different country or are already in a new region. If that all sounds OK to you, here's how to change your Xbox region to New Zealand ( via Insider Gaming ). Go to Settings Click System, then Language & Localization Switch your location to New Zealand Restart your console The process of changing regions on PlayStation 5 is not as straightforward and involves numerous other steps-- Insider Gaming has a rundown. However, it's also been reported that players changing their PS5 region have begun receiving account suspensions without warning. GTA 6 launches on November 19, but midnight in New Zealand on November 19 is 3 AM PT / 6 AM ET on November 18. So people in the US will have to wait a very long time to play GTA 6 compared to the people who live in New Zealand. For more on GTA 6, including preload information, preorder bonuses, and release times, check out our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.
